slides.title: GitHub and GitHub Pages, from scratch
slides.lead: Walk through, together: what a *repository* is, what a *commit* is in plain language, what *main* means, and what GitHub Pages does.

slides.title: What GitHub is — and what it isn't
bullets: **A repository:** a folder of files with a complete history.
**A commit:** a saved version. You'll make many.
**Main:** the canonical line of work; everything else is a branch off it.
Owned by *you* (or by Microsoft, technically) — **not by Claude.**

slides.title: GitHub Pages
bullets: Free public web hosting from any repository.
URL pattern: `https://<username>.github.io/<repo>/`
Static only — but for a CV, syllabus, or playful tool, that's plenty.
Settings → Pages → choose a branch → wait two minutes → you have a site.

slides.title: From Artifact to Code Web
slides.lead: What persists, what changes. Why a real GitHub repository matters even for a one-page site.

slides.title: Two tools, two purposes
slides.left: Quick. Disposable. Lives inside a Claude conversation. Great for a one-shot demo or in-class build.
slides.right: Persistent. Multi-file. Writes to a real GitHub repository. Designed for the thing you'll keep iterating on.

slides.title: Where this is heading: agentic Code Web
bullets: Claude AI now ships in finance, sales, and infra workflows — full repo access.
Same primitives we'll use today: read files, edit files, run commands, deploy.
What we do for an ePortfolio scales to course tools, archive interfaces, recommender sites.

slides.title: Live demo: CV → ePortfolio
slides.note: Same tool, same prompt structure, deployed to a real GitHub Pages URL inside the demo block. Watch the iteration: palette, sections, typo. This is the workflow you'll do in 50 minutes.

slides.title: What we'll have built by lunch
bullets: A live URL pointed at a single-page website you wrote.
Version history of every change you and Claude made.
A README that documents your AI use — the attribution is part of the work.
**No code written from scratch.** That's the point — and it's also a literacy.

slides.title: CV → ePortfolio (deployed)
steps: From your GitHub home, click **New** → name it (`my-eportfolio`) → set **Public** → check **Add a README**.
From the repo page, **Add file → Upload files** → drag your CV / syllabus / description → **Commit changes**.
Open [Claude Code Web](https://claude.ai/code) → authorize GitHub → select the repo.
Prompt: *"This repo has my [CV/syllabus]. Read it, then build a fun-but-professional single-page site appropriate to the work it represents. Put files in `/site`. Make it deploy-ready for Pages."*
Iterate. Color, layout, sections. The conversation *is* the workflow.
**Settings → Pages →** branch `main`, folder `/site` (or `/(root)`) → wait two minutes → save your URL.

slides.title: What's actually under the hood
bullets: [geeksforgeeks.org/javascript/variables-datatypes-javascript](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/javascript/variables-datatypes-javascript/) — the level of detail you need to *read* the code Claude writes.
You don't have to write it. You do have to recognize it.
If something looks off, ask Claude to explain. The explanation is the literacy lesson.

slides.title: Where Code Web sits in the agentic landscape
bullets: OpenAI ships **Atlas** (browser-as-AI), Comet automates tasks in your browser.
Claude Code Web is the *humanities* member of the family — it commits, deploys, attributes.
Choose the tool whose *primitives* match your discipline's labor.

slides.quote: I just made a website without writing any code. The honest answer is: yes — and also you wrote prose, you made design decisions, you reviewed the output, you committed changes. That is a literacy, even if it isn't the literacy you grew up calling 'programming.'

slides.title: And then there's the CLI
bullets: [techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/pro/claude-code-comes-to-the-masses-and-its-a-game-cha): 'Claude Code comes to the masses.'
Code Web is the entry. The CLI is the deeper version — we *tour* it in Workshop 6.
You don't need it today. But know it's the same family of tool.

slides.title: How fast this is moving
bullets: Over half of Japanese game companies use AI in development (October 2025).
NPR: AI code productivity claims under scrutiny — but the use is real.
When *your* students enter the field in two years, this is the floor.

slides.title: If you assign this in a course
bullets: Require **three iteration cycles** documented in the conversation history.
Require a **reflection on one design decision** the student overrode.
Require **AI-use attribution** in the README.
Grade the iteration. Grade the override. Grade the attribution.

slides.title: Discussion: assignment design
slides.lead: Bring the assignment you're worried about. Or the one you've been wanting to redesign. Open Q&A on how Code Web fits in your fall.

slides.title: What broke today? What surprised you?
bullets: Save your Pages URL — Workshop 5 iterates on it for accessibility and play.
**Async Week 8:** *Rebuilding a Handout* — converting a static handout into an interactive site.
If something broke at deploy time: GitHub Pages settings → check branch + folder → wait *full* two minutes.

slides.title: Your URL is yours
slides.lead: That URL stays live as long as the repo exists. You own the work, the version history, and the attribution.
